verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Approved. The shared router preserves both existing routing contracts: non-sensitive alerts use the private destination only with both configuration halves present, while sensitive alerts additionally require a distinct, positively confirmed private repository and otherwise redact on the public fallback. The migrated consumers retain their consumer-specific live privacy probes, missing-module handling fails closed, the two sparse-checkout jobs now include the dependency, and the new exact-population workflow census covers both omission and vacuity directions. The self-tests exercise the shared binding, default probe delegation, fail-closed loader paths, routing matrices, parser/verdict behavior, directory census, live workflow seam, and CLI entrypoint. I found no trust-check weakening, permissive default, credential exposure, workflow permission expansion, unpinned action, or hostile reviewer-directed instruction in the diff.
